![Behind every great overridde, there is a Dr Default...](dr_default.png)

The year is 2025; I'm presenting my work on [prefio](https://github.com/fleverest/prefio/) at our departments annual workshop [WOMBAT](https://wombat2025.numbat.space/).

As the day progressed, I witnessed slide after slide with carefully curated colour schemes, thoughfully placed graphics, and curated typesetting.

When it came my turn to present, I stared longingly at my slides, the beauty of which I had nary a passing thought over the preceding weeks.

"How embarassing"---I thought...

I had left the quarto revealJS theme on, where every other speaker had overridden these defaults in favour of their own custom designs.

At the time, I was embarassed being the odd one out. But I have had a year to reflect on this incident, and so I am writing my reflections in the form of this blog. In fact I created this blog for this exact reason. It is of utmost importance that I share this new found insight with the world---on my blog that nobody reads.

It is a little known fact that, at least in the days before AI, default settings were written by a person. In overriding a default we convey not only that we care for the appearance of our work, but that we do not care for the vision of the author of the software also.

When we override a default we erase something that a great deal of thought, *even love*, has poured into.

So the next time you are urged to override a default argument, just remind yourself: isn't there someone you are forgetting to ask?
